chief_complaint: fear of abandonment, unstable identity, wrist cutting
hpi_details: A 50-year-old woman presents to the clinic with fear of abandonment, unstable identity, and wrist cutting. She describes this as a pattern she has lived with since her late teens — intense and unstable relationships, chronic emptiness, and repeated self-injury around separations — which has flared again over the past few weeks since her partner moved out, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she has a fundamental defect that makes her impossible to love and dooms every relationship she cares about.
concerns: She is worried that the unbearable emptiness since her partner walked out will push her to cut too deep during a breakdown.
expectations: She hopes to be connected with a counselor who will not abandon her and to receive medication to dull the crushing emotional agony.
pmh: Long-standing pattern of unstable relationships, chronic emptiness, and recurrent self-harm dating back to late adolescence; several brief contacts with mental health services, no psychiatric admission

history.answer: I've been feeling overwhelmed and deeply depressed, and a couple of days ago I ended up cutting my wrist again after my partner left me.
My low mood flared intensely about three weeks ago right after my partner moved out, though my feelings fluctuate wildly throughout every day.
history.topic: Onset and course of low mood

history.answer: Three weeks ago, my partner packed their bags and walked out after an argument, which completely shattered me.
I haven't been able to enjoy anything lately. Everything feels empty and pointless right now.
It takes me hours to fall asleep because my mind races with panic, but in the mornings I struggle to get out of bed.
My appetite has dropped significantly over the past three weeks, and I think I've lost about two kilograms.
I feel constantly drained and fatigued, and my concentration is so poor that I can barely focus on work or reading.
I feel completely worthless and broken, like everything that goes wrong in my relationships is entirely my fault.
I feel emotionally agitated and restless inside, pacing back and forth whenever the wave of panic hits.
I made several shallow cuts on my left wrist two days ago with a razor blade. It was not to end my life, but to release the unbearable emotional agony inside.
I have had passing thoughts that maybe not waking up would end the pain, but I do not want to die and have no plan or intention to commit suicide.
My sister checks on me every evening, and I genuinely want to learn how to heal and stop destroying my life.
I'm terrified that one night the pain and emptiness will get so bad that I'll cut too deep and bleed to death all alone.
My relationships are always turbulent. I tend to see people as either perfect angels or completely heartless, and my feelings switch in an instant.
I have never known who I truly am. My sense of self, career goals, and values keep shifting depending on who I am around.
There is a profound, aching void inside my chest that has been there for as long as I can remember.
I struggle with intense, explosive anger over minor slights, and I say awful things that I immediately regret once I calm down.
When I am distressed, I do reckless things without thinking, like spending money I don't have, binge eating, or cutting myself.
I don't have intrusive flashbacks or nightmares of a life-threatening trauma.
No, I have never had times where I felt unusually high, needed almost no sleep, or felt grandiose.
No, I have never heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or felt that anyone was persecuting me.
This crisis has disrupted my entire routine. I called in sick to work all week and have barely left my apartment.
No, I haven't had cold intolerance, coarse hair, or constipation.
I have struggled with emotional volatility, turbulent relationships, and self-harm since my late teens, but I have no other chronic medical illnesses.
I have attended brief counseling sessions and seen a psychiatrist a couple of times over the years, but I have never been admitted to a psychiatric hospital.
I had an uncomplicated appendectomy in my early twenties, but no other surgeries or hospitalizations.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or supplements right now.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I do not smoke cigarettes or use any nicotine products.
I only drink socially, maybe a glass of wine once or twice a month, and I do not use illicit drugs.
I work as an administrative assistant at an office, and I live alone in an apartment now that my partner has left.
My cycles have become somewhat irregular over the past year, and my last menstrual period was about two months ago. I am not pregnant.
My mother struggled with severe chronic depression and mood swings, but there is no family history of completed suicide or bipolar disorder.
I feel like there's something fundamentally broken inside me that makes me impossible to love and drives everyone away.
I'm terrified that one night the pain and emptiness will get so bad that I'll cut too deep and bleed to death all alone.
I'm hoping to get a referral to a long-term therapist who won't give up on me and something to take the edge off this agonizing pain.
